title: A comprehensive view of the interstellar medium in a quasar host galaxy at z ≈ 6.4
question: Characterize the global physical properties, gas phases (ionized, neutral, molecular), excitation mechanisms, and mass budget of the star-forming interstellar medium in the quasar host galaxy PSO J183.1124+05.0926 at z=6.4386.

what.value: Deconvolved dust sizes (0.45'' x 0.35'') and spatial extent of PJ183+05 at rest-frame 88 um

evidence.quote: Two-dimensional channel-by-channel fits of the quasar emission at 88 $\mu$m in the rest-frame revealed that the emission is spatially unresolved or only marginally resolved at $>0.7''$ resolution (cite: venemans20).

For the angular size, $\Omega_{\rm s}$, we adopt a Gaussian distribution around the spatial extent reported in (cite: venemans20) (deconvolved dust sizes: $0.45''\times0.35'' \approx 2.4\times 1.9$ kpc$^2$).

what.value: Dust emissivity law values at nu_0 > 1500 GHz

evidence.quote: $\kappa(\nu_0)$ is the dust emissivity law, for which we adopt an interpolation of the values reported in Table 5 of (cite: draine03) at $\nu_0>1500$ GHz
and $\Omega(l,u)$ are the collision strengths, which we take from Appendix F of (cite: draine11).

what.value: Empirical relation between [N II]205um/[C II]158um and dust color C(60/100)

evidence.loc: Inferred [N ii]205 um and the origin of [C ii]
evidence.quote: We estimate the luminosity of the \[N ii\]$_{\rm 205\,\mu m}$ line following the empirical trend presented in (cite: lu15) for a sample of local luminous IR galaxies:

recipe.goal: Extract single-pixel spectra and fit emission lines and continuum
recipe.method: Single-pixel spectral extraction at the quasar position, followed by MCMC fitting of a flat continuum plus a fixed-width Gaussian profile for each targeted line.
software: custom Monte Carlo Markov Chain tool
assumptions: All lines have the same Gaussian width of 375 km/s as [C II]

recipe.goal: Model the dust continuum SED and derive dust properties, IR luminosity, and optical depth
recipe.method: Fit a modified black body observed against the CMB and corrected for radiative transfer (optical depth) using MCMC, then integrate over 8-1000 um for L_IR.
key_parameters: Four free parameters: T_dust, Omega_s, M_dust, beta
assumptions: Dust emissivity law from Draine (2003) at nu_0 > 1500 GHz and power-law extrapolation kappa(nu_0) = 6.37 (nu_0/1500 GHz)^beta cm^2 g^-1 at lower frequencies

recipe.goal: Model emission lines using analytical first-principles prescriptions and Cloudy simulations
recipe.method: Solve linear statistical equilibrium equations for level populations in ionized gas and run Cloudy photoionization, PDR, and XDR slab models across grids of density, metallicity, and radiation fields.
key_parameters: Ionized grid: fixed log U = -2, log n [cm^-3] = [0, +3] (step 0.25 dex), log Z [Z_sun] = [-1, +0.4] (step 0.2 dex), turbulence RMS = 100 km/s, stopping at x_HI = 0.05
PDR/XDR grid: log n [cm^-3] = [2, 6] (0.29 dex spacing), log G_0 = [1, 6] (0.29 dex spacing) or log F_X = [-2.0, 2.0] (0.24 dex spacing), log N_H [cm^-2] = [22, 24] (1 dex spacing)
assumptions: Constant density throughout each cloud; three distinct components (ionized, neutral, molecular)
Abundance scaling from Nicholls et al. (2017)

recipe.goal: Infer [N II] 205 um luminosity, PDR fraction of [C II], electron density, H II volume, and radiation field hardness
recipe.method: Estimate [N II] 205 um from dust color C(60/100) via Lu et al. (2015), compare with [C II] and [N II] 122 um to derive f([C II]^PDR), electron density n, H II region volume, and compare [O III]/[N II] with Cloudy grids for radiation hardness.
assumptions: No dust opacity correction applied to fiducial line luminosities; solar metallicity Z = Z_sun and T_gas = 10,000 K for H II volume

recipe.goal: Estimate ionized and molecular gas masses and star formation rates from multiple tracers
recipe.method: Calculate ionized and molecular gas masses from level populations, dust mass, CO(7-6), [C I], and [C II]^PDR, and compute SFR from [O III], [C II], and IR luminosity using empirical scaling relations.
assumptions: Gas-to-dust ratio delta_g/d = 100, alpha_CO = 0.8 M_sun (K km s^-1 pc^2)^-1, CO line ratio r_71 = 0.38 (for mass) or 0.20 (inferred from dust), T_ex = T_gas, Z = Z_sun

evidence.quote: Compared to the observed CO(7-6) luminosity, $L'_{\rm CO(7-6)}=(2.16\pm0.24)\times 10^{11}$ K km s$^{-1}$ pc$^2$, this implies a line ratio $r_{71}=L'_{\rm CO(7-6)}/L'_{\rm CO(1-0)}$ = 0.20.

evidence.quote: Using the measured \[N ii\]$_{122\,\mu{\rm m}}$ luminosity from Tab. \[\[tab_lines\]\](#tab_lines), and the inferred \[N ii\]$_{205\,\mu{\rm m}}$ from the previous section, we find a ratio of $\log$\[N ii\]$_{122\,\mu{\rm m}}$/\[N ii\]$_{205\,\mu{\rm m}}$=$0.56_{-0.16}^{+0.23}$, corresponding to a gas density of $\log n$ \[cm$^{-3}$\] $=2.26\pm 0.35$.

evidence.loc: Electron density and size of the Hii regions
evidence.quote: For $T_{\rm gas}=10,000$ K, $n$=180 cm$^{-3}$, and Z=Z$_\odot$, using eq. \[\[eq_Lc_model\]\](#eq_Lc_model) in the case of the \[N ii\]$_{122\,\mu{\rm m}}$ transition, we obtain an effective volume of the ionized gas, $V_{\rm HII}^{\rm eff}\sim 0.2$ kpc$^3$.
Here we measure a ratio of $\log$ \[C ii\]/\[C i\] = $1.55_{-0.13}^{+0.17}$.
We find that the low-ionization species (\[C ii\], \[N ii\]) yield very consistent ionized gas mass estimates, $M_{\rm HII}=(2-3)\times 10^{10}$ M$_\odot$.
